args: updown topranking --help
exit: 0
--- stdout
Get pseudo-phylogenetic-tree-aware neighbours by genetic distance from alignments

Example usage:
	gofasta updown topranking --query smallquery.fasta -r WH04.fasta --target mutationlist.csv --size-total 1000 -o catchment.csv

For each sequence in --query, this routine finds the closest sequences by SNP-distance in --target, binned
according to whether they are likely children, parents, siblings of, or on a polytomy with, the query
sequence. It does this by comparing SNPs relative to a common sequence which is imagined to be the
root of the tree.

--query and --target can either be alignments in fasta format, or the CSV output of gofasta updown list, or
one of each; which is worked out from their content, so they can be called anything, and either (but not both)
can be stdin. If either is an alignment, you must provide --root. If only one is an alignment, --root must be
the same sequence that was used by gofasta updown list to generate the other file.

Use --dist-all, or --dist-up, --dist-down and --dist-side, to filter on SNP-distances in each direction. As
long as you haven't also used any of the --size-* flags (--size-total, --size-up, --size-down, --size-side,
--size-same), the program will return all the targets that are equal or less than the specified
SNP-distance(s) away. With only some of --dist-up, --dist-down and --dist-side, only those bins are returned,
and the same bin, whose targets are always 0 SNPs away. If --dist-push is invoked with an integer (i)
argument, the program will push the SNP-distance boundaries outwards, where needed, so that each bin covers at
least the closest i SNP-distances at which it has neighbours, and then it will return all the neighbours
within the boundary in that bin. Only the bins with a --dist-* value are pushed (up, down and side with
--dist-all); without any --dist-* flags, all three are pushed from 0, so each has the neighbours at its
closest i SNP-distances.

If you provide a number to --size-total, the output will try to include this many closest sequences to the
query, split evenly between the four bins. If one or more bins has a shortfall, the sizes of the other bins
will increase until --size-total is met, if possible, unless you use --no-fill.

You can provide --size-up, --size-down, --size-side and --size-same, instead of --size-total, if you want
different proportions for each bin. The program will aim to provide the sum of these numbers in total in the
output, and will make up for a shortfall in one bin by increasing the count of the other bins where possible,
unless --no-fill.

You can combine the two types of flag (--size-* and --dist-*), to return only the closest n sequences under a
set distance (as long as you haven't also invoked --dist-push).

Usage:
  gofasta updown topranking [flags]

Flags:
      --query string             File with sequences to find neighbours for. Either the CSV output of gofasta updown list, or an alignment in fasta format (required)
      --target string            File of sequences to look for neighbours in. Either the CSV output of gofasta updown list, or an alignment in fasta format (required)
      --ignore string            Plain text file of IDs of --target sequences to ignore when searching for neighbours
  -r, --root string              Root sequence, in fasta format (required if --query or --target is a fasta file)
  -o, --outfile string           Where to write the closest neighbours, in CSV format (default "stdout")
      --table                    Write a long-form table of the output
      --size-total int           Max number of neighbours to find (attempts to split equally between same/up/down/side). A hard limit
      --size-up int              Max number of closest parent sequences to find, if --size-total is not given. A soft limit unless --no-fill
      --size-down int            Max number of closest child sequences to find, if --size-total is not given. A soft limit unless --no-fill
      --size-side int            Max number of closest sibling sequences to find, if --size-total is not given. A soft limit unless --no-fill
      --size-same int            Max number of identical sequences to find, if --size-total is not given. A soft limit unless --no-fill
      --no-fill                  Don't make up for a shortfall in any of --size-up, --size-down, --size-side or --size-same by increasing the count for other bins
      --dist-all int             Maximum allowed SNP-distance between a --query and a --target sequence in any direction. Overrides the settings below
      --dist-up int              Maximum allowed SNP-distance from query for sequences in the parent bin
      --dist-down int            Maximum allowed SNP-distance from query for sequences in the child bin
      --dist-side int            Maximum allowed SNP-distance from query for sequences in the sibling bin
      --dist-push int            Push the --dist-all, --dist-up, --dist-down and --dist-side boundaries outwards so that bins have at least these many closest SNP-distances for which there are neighbours, where possible
      --threshold-pair float32   Up to this proportion of consequential sites is allowed to be ambiguous in either sequence for each pairwise comparison (default 0.1)
      --threshold-target int     A --target sequence can have at most this number of ambiguities to be considered (default 10000)
      --strict                   Stop with an error at the first record that can't be processed, instead of warning and skipping it
  -t, --threads int              Number of threads (and CPUs) to use (with no flag, all CPUs are used)
  -h, --help                     help for topranking
--- stderr
